stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mtext>active</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mtext>inactive</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{ij}\mid z_{i},z_{j}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\pi_{\mathrm{int}}\cdot z_{i}z_{j}),\qquad\beta_{ij}\mid z_{ij},\sigma^{2}\sim\begin{cases}\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}\tau_{\text{active}}^{2}),&amp;z_{ij}=1,\\
\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}\tau_{\text{inactive}}^{2}),&amp;z_{ij}=0.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.3" class="ltx_p">Strong heredity is a modelling assumption. Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Ablations and robustness ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> reports an ablation that relaxes it and quantifies the sensitivity of the recovered active set. The expected response is modeled as a linear combination of all active effects:</p>
<table id="S3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(\xi_{t},\theta)=\sum_{k=1}^{p}z_{k}\beta_{k}\xi_{t,k}+\sum_{i&lt;j}z_{ij}\beta_{ij}\xi_{t,i}\xi_{t,j}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>p</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(\xi_{t},\theta)=\sum_{k=1}^{p}z_{k}\beta_{k}\xi_{t,k}+\sum_{i&lt;j}z_{ij}\beta_{ij}\xi_{t,i}\xi_{t,j}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.4" class="ltx_p">The formulation captures two key properties of screening experiments: the sparsity of active factors and structured interactions through the heredity constraint. Under heredity, the space of admissible activity patterns reduces from <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0,1\}^{p+p(p-1)/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0,1\}^{p+p(p-1)/2}</annotation></semantics></math> to at most <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0,1\}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0,1\}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math>. For instance, when <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=15</annotation></semantics></math>, this is a reduction from <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{120}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>120</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{120}</annotation></semantics></math> to at most <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{15}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>15</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{15}</annotation></semantics></math> distinct configurations, a reduction of at least 31 orders of magnitude. This reduction, induced by the strong heredity assumption, is critical for scalability as it renders the contrastive sPCE objective tractable: contrastive samples need only be drawn from at most <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0,1\}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0,1\}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math> rather than the full joint space.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Analytical Marginalisation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The screening model of Section 3.1 decomposes the parameter
vector as <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=(z,\beta,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=(z,\beta,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=((z_{k})_{k=1}^{p},(z_{ij})_{i&lt;j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>p</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=((z_{k})_{k=1}^{p},(z_{ij})_{i&lt;j})</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the joint activity indicators, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> the continuous effect sizes for main effects and heredity-constrained interactions, and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> the observation noise
variance. Under the Gaussian likelihood of Eq. <a href="#S3.E6" title="In 3.1 Problem Setup and Factorial Screening Model ‣ 3 Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and the
conjugate normal–inverse-gamma prior on <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> induced by
the spike-and-slab specification in Eq. <a href="#S3.E7" title="In 3.1 Problem Setup and Factorial Screening Model ‣ 3 Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> together with the inverse-gamma prior on <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, the continuous parameters admit
closed-form integration. Conditioned on <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, the joint distribution of the
history <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{T}=\{(\xi_{t},y_{t})\}_{t=1}^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{T}=\{(\xi_{t},y_{t})\}_{t=1}^{T}</annotation></semantics></math> follows a multivariate
Student-<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> distribution</p>
<table id="S3.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(h_{T}\mid z)\;=\;\iint p(h_{T}\mid z,\beta,\sigma^{2})\,p(\beta\mid z,\sigma^{2})\,p(\sigma^{2})\,d\beta\,d\sigma^{2}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.391em">=</mo><mrow><mo>∬</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(h_{T}\mid z)\;=\;\iint p(h_{T}\mid z,\beta,\sigma^{2})\,p(\beta\mid z,\sigma^{2})\,p(\sigma^{2})\,d\beta\,d\sigma^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">whose scale matrix and degrees of freedom are determined by the active set
<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, the design matrix induced by the history, and the prior hyperparameters
<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{0},\beta_{0},\tau^{2}_{\mathrm{active}},\tau^{2}_{\mathrm{inactive}},\pi_{\mathrm{int}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>active</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>inactive</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>int</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{0},\beta_{0},\tau^{2}_{\mathrm{active}},\tau^{2}_{\mathrm{inactive}},\pi_{\mathrm{int}})</annotation></semantics></math>.
The full derivation is provided in Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Derivation of the joint distribution of the history ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This analytical marginalization has two consequences for training. First, the sPCE objective (Eq. <a href="#S2.E4" title="In 2.2 Contrastive Estimation of Information Gain ‣ 2 Background ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) specializes naturally: contrastive samples need only be drawn from <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z)</annotation></semantics></math> over the discrete activity indicators, with each trajectory likelihood <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(h_{T}\mid z_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(h_{T}\mid z_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> evaluated via the closed-form Student-<math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> marginal. Second, because <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> never appear in the contrastive draws, the Monte Carlo variance of the estimator does not inflate with the dimension of the continuous parameters, keeping the training signal stable as <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> increases.
The resulting estimator therefore targets the cumulative mutual information <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(z;h_{T}\mid\pi_{\phi})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(z;h_{T}\mid\pi_{\phi})</annotation></semantics></math> between the activity indicators and the trajectory under the policy, rather than the full <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(\theta;h_{T}\mid\pi_{\phi})=\mathcal{J}(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\theta;h_{T}\mid\pi_{\phi})=\mathcal{J}(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math> used in DAD-style methods. This concentrates the training signal on the discrete screening decision. The continuous parameters <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> are integrated out analytically during training and recovered exactly at deployment via the closed-form Gibbs sampler.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Learning the Adaptive Design Policy</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The conjugate linear–Gaussian structure yields a closed-form marginal likelihood, eliminating the need for variational bounds or nested Monte Carlo estimators typically required in Bayesian optimal experimental design. As a result, policy learning reduces to direct maximization of the sPCE objective using standard gradient-based methods.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">However, the designs <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{t}\in\{-1,+1\}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{t}\in\{-1,+1\}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math> are discrete. Therefore, pathwise gradient estimators cannot be applied directly. To enable end-to-end training while preserving discrete designs at evaluation, we employ a straight-through Gumbel–Softmax relaxation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jang et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maddison et al., 2017</a>)</cite>. At each step, the policy network outputs logits <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}=\pi_{\phi}(h_{t-1})\in\mathbb{R}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}=\pi_{\phi}(h_{t-1})\in\mathbb{R}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, and a design is sampled as</p>
<table id="S3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{t}=\mathrm{sign}(\ell_{t}+g_{t}),\quad g_{t}\sim\mathrm{Gumbel}(0,\tau)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>sign</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Gumbel</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{t}=\mathrm{sign}(\ell_{t}+g_{t}),\quad g_{t}\sim\mathrm{Gumbel}(0,\tau),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">with temperature <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> annealed from <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{start}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>start</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{start}}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{end}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>end</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{end}}</annotation></semantics></math> during training. The forward pass uses the discrete <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{-1,+1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{-1,+1\}</annotation></semantics></math> designs for likelihood evaluation, while the backward pass propagates gradients through the continuous relaxation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tucker et al., 2017</a>)</cite>. At evaluation time, Gumbel noise is removed and logits are thresholded at zero, yielding deterministic <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{-1,+1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{-1,+1\}</annotation></semantics></math> designs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Because the history <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> grows with <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we compress it into fixed-dimensional sufficient statistics before passing it to the policy. Specifically, we map <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1},X_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1},y_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1},X_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1},y_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1})</annotation></semantics></math>, which fully determine the Student-<math id="S3.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> posterior under the conjugate prior, through a two-hidden-layer multilayer perceptron (MLP) that outputs the logits <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. This representation is exactly sufficient for Bayesian inference under the linear–Gaussian likelihood and yields a more sample-efficient policy than set-equivariant encoders applied directly to the raw <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\xi_{s},y_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\xi_{s},y_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> pairs. The encoder architecture and a formal sufficiency argument are given in Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Encoder details ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">A practical failure mode in sequential design policies is collapse, where the policy repeatedly selects identical or highly similar designs across steps, effectively ignoring the adaptive nature of the task <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Crombecq et al., 2011</a>)</cite>. In screening, this is particularly problematic: repeating the same design provides no additional information, as observations are conditionally independent given <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. Empirically, optimizing sPCE alone does not prevent collapse, since increasing logit magnitudes drive the softmax toward a degenerate deterministic policy long before exploration has resolved the posterior over <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">To mitigate this, we add a squared-<math id="S3.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> penalty on the policy logits <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fanuel et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Schreurs et al., 2022</a>)</cite>:
<math id="S3.SS3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{L2}(\phi)=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\ell_{t}\|_{2}^{2}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{L2}(\phi)=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\ell_{t}\|_{2}^{2},</annotation></semantics></math> which keeps logits bounded and preserves Gumbel-induced exploration throughout training. The full objective is</p>
<table id="S3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(\phi)=-\widehat{\text{sPCE}}_{L}(\phi)+\mu\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{L2}}(\phi)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mtext>sPCE</mtext><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>L2</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(\phi)=-\widehat{\text{sPCE}}_{L}(\phi)+\mu\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{L2}}(\phi),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p5.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> controls the trade-off between information gain and policy regularization. We minimize <math id="S3.SS3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math> via stochastic gradient descent, which is equivalent to maximizing the sPCE lower bound subject to an <math id="S3.SS3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> penalty on the policy logits. Adding the penalty does shift the stationary points of the combined objective, but its strength grows with the logit magnitude, so it acts primarily in the runaway-logit regime that leads to collapse. Because identical designs carry no additional information under conditional independence, a policy that maximizes <math id="S3.SS3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{J}(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{J}(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math> naturally produces diverse designs with moderate logit magnitudes, for which the penalty is negligible. Its role is therefore to prevent the large-logit collapse to which Gumbel-Softmax training is prone, rather than to trade off information gain. The full training procedure is summarized in the pseudo code in Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Pseudo-code of the training procedure ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Policy Network Architecture</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Having defined the policy optimization procedure, we now describe the parametrization of the design policy <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\phi}(\xi_{t}\mid h_{t-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi}(\xi_{t}\mid h_{t-1})</annotation></semantics></math>. The policy must map a variable-length history of experiment-outcome pairs to the next design, with two structural requirements: (i) invariance to the order of past experiments and (ii) accommodation of histories of growing length.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In the screening setting, observations are conditionally independent given the true parameters, <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}\perp h_{t-1}\mid\theta,\xi_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>⟂</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}\perp h_{t-1}\mid\theta,\xi_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. As shown by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Foster et al. (2021)</a></cite>, this implies that the optimal policy depends only on the multiset of past <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\xi_{s},y_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\xi_{s},y_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> pairs, not their order. We exploit this structure by basing <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> on the sufficient statistics of the linear–Gaussian likelihood, which are permutation-invariant by construction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Given history <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> with expanded design matrix <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{(t-1)\times d_{\mathrm{full}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>full</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{(t-1)\times d_{\mathrm{full}}}</annotation></semantics></math> (main-effect columns plus two-factor interaction columns) and response vector <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute</p>
<table id="S3.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t-1}=\bigl(\operatorname{vec}(X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1}),\;X_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1},\;y_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1}\bigr)\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{\mathrm{full}}(d_{\mathrm{full}}+1)}{2}+d_{\mathrm{full}}+1}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>full</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>full</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>full</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t-1}=\bigl(\operatorname{vec}(X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1}),\;X_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1},\;y_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1}\bigr)\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{\mathrm{full}}(d_{\mathrm{full}}+1)}{2}+d_{\mathrm{full}}+1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{full}}=p+p(p-1)/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>full</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{full}}=p+p(p-1)/2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{vec}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{vec}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> extracts the upper-triangular entries of the symmetric matrix <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. These statistics are exactly sufficient for the Student-<math id="S3.SS4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> posterior over <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> under the conjugate Normal–Inverse-Gamma prior (Section 3.2), and their dimension is constant in <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The policy logits are produced by a single MLP:
<math id="S3.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}=\mu_{\phi}(s_{t-1},t)\in\mathbb{R}^{p}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}=\mu_{\phi}(s_{t-1},t)\in\mathbb{R}^{p},</annotation></semantics></math>
where <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is a scalar positional index appended to the input. The MLP <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> has two hidden layers with Softplus activations and applies dropout during training to prevent logit saturation. From <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, the design <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{t}\in\{-1,+1\}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{t}\in\{-1,+1\}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math> is produced via the straight-through Gumbel-Softmax mechanism described in Section 3.3.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">This design has two key properties. Permutation invariance over past experiments holds by construction, since the statistics in Eq. <a href="#S3.E13" title="In 3.4 Policy Network Architecture ‣ 3 Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> are symmetric functions of the <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\xi_{s},y_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\xi_{s},y_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> pairs. Moreover, <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> is the only trainable component of the system: leveraging the closed-form Student-<math id="S3.SS4.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> marginal, the contrastive objective (Eq. <a href="#S2.E4" title="In 2.2 Contrastive Estimation of Information Gain ‣ 2 Background ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) can be evaluated analytically, without requiring a separate utility or critic network. As a result, training reduces to backpropagating a single likelihood-based loss through a single MLP, avoiding the instabilities often associated with multi-network adversarial training. Figure <a href="#S3.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 3.5 Posterior Inference and Deployment ‣ 3 Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>(a) provides a visual overview.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5 </span>Posterior Inference and Deployment</h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following the completion of <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> adaptive experiments, the collected history <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> is used to identify the active factors and estimate their effects via the posterior distribution <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(z,\beta\mid h_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z,\beta\mid h_{T})</annotation></semantics></math>. Unlike prior policy-based BOED methods, which focus solely on design, DABS integrates posterior inference into deployment, enabling both variable selection and posterior uncertainty quantification.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Direct posterior computation is intractable due to the discrete nature of <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\in\{0,1\}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\in\{0,1\}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math>. We therefore employ a Gibbs sampler <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">George and McCulloch, 1993</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Geman and Geman, 1984</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">George and McCulloch, 1997</a>)</cite> that alternates between sampling <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,\sigma^{2})\mid z,h_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta,\sigma^{2})\mid z,h_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\mid\beta,\sigma^{2},h_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\mid\beta,\sigma^{2},h_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, all available in closed form under the conjugate Normal–Inverse-Gamma g-prior and
Gaussian likelihood (see Algorithm 2 in Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Pseudo-code of the full deployment and inference pipeline ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a> for the full deployment pipeline, and Appendix <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Posterior inference details ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a> for the Gibbs step-by-step details).
The primary outputs are the posterior activity probabilities and effect size estimates:</p>
<table id="S3.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}(z_{k}=1\mid h_{T})=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}z_{k}^{(g)},\qquad\hat{\beta}_{k}=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}\beta_{k}^{(g)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>G</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>G</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>β</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}(z_{k}=1\mid h_{T})=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}z_{k}^{(g)},\qquad\hat{\beta}_{k}=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}\beta_{k}^{(g)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.2" class="ltx_p">with analogous expressions for the interaction indicators <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math> and effects <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>β</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math>. A factor (or interaction) is declared active if <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}(z_{k}=1\mid h_{T})&gt;0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}(z_{k}=1\mid h_{T})&gt;0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, and uncertainty is quantified via posterior credible intervals. The full inference procedure is summarized in Figure <a href="#S3.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 3.5 Posterior Inference and Deployment ‣ 3 Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>(b).</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>(a) DABS policy network <math id="S3.F1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> and (b) deployment with Gibbs posterior inference.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.6 </span>When Does Adaptivity Help </h3>

<div id="S3.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The screening model of Sections 3.1–3.2 decomposes <math id="S3.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=(z,\beta,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=(z,\beta,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> into discrete activity indicators, continuous effect sizes, and the noise variance. This decomposition determines which component of <math id="S3.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> carries the adaptive gain and which does not.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">By the chain rule of mutual information, the total information the experimental history <math id="S3.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> carries about <math id="S3.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> factorises as</p>
<table id="S3.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(\theta;h_{T})=I(z;h_{T})+\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\left[I(\beta,\sigma^{2};h_{T}\mid z)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\theta;h_{T})=I(z;h_{T})+\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\left[I(\beta,\sigma^{2};h_{T}\mid z)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS6.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The first term measures information about the discrete active-set indicators. The second measures information about the effect sizes and noise variance conditional on the active set. The sPCE objective used by DABS (Eq. <a href="#S2.E4" title="In 2.2 Contrastive Estimation of Information Gain ‣ 2 Background ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) targets the first term via the analytical Student-<math id="S3.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> marginalisation of Section 3.2, integrating out <math id="S3.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A classical result on Bayesian experimental design in linear-Gaussian likelihoods <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lindley, 1955</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chaloner and Verdinelli, 1995</a>)</cite> establishes that the posterior covariance of <math id="S3.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> given <math id="S3.SS6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> depends only on the design matrix and not on the observed responses. The conditional information gain <math id="S3.SS6.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(\beta,\sigma^{2};h_{T}\mid z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\beta,\sigma^{2};h_{T}\mid z)</annotation></semantics></math> is therefore a function of the design matrix alone: an optimal non-adaptive design achieves the same conditional information gain as any adaptive policy at equal budget. All adaptive leverage in Eq. <a href="#S3.E15" title="In 3.6 When Does Adaptivity Help ‣ 3 Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> flows through the first term, <math id="S3.SS6.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(z;h_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(z;h_{T})</annotation></semantics></math>. 
<br class="ltx_break">
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S3.SS6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:258.4pt;">

-14.28)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:1em;--ltx-fo-height:0.57em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:7.97pt;" height="6.24" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 6.24)" width="11.03"><span style="fill:none" d="M 0 39.37 L -3.15 39.37"></path><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -13.55 36.25)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.5em;--ltx-fo-height:0.57em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:7.97pt;" height="6.24" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 6.24)" width="5.52"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S3.SS6.p3.pic1.14" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">5</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><path style="fill:none" d="M 0 78.74 L -3.15 78.74"></path><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -19.07 75.62)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:1em;--ltx-fo-height:0.57em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:7.97pt;" height="6.24" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 6.24)" width="11.03"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S3.SS6.p3.pic1.15" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">10</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><path style="fill:none" d="M 0 118.11 L -3.15 118.11"></path><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -19.07 114.99)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:1em;--ltx-fo-height:0.57em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:7.97pt;" height="6.24" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 6.24)" width="11.03"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S3.SS6.p3.pic1.16" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">15</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><path style="fill:none" d="M 0 157.48 L -3.15 157.48"></path><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -19.07
