<tr id="A2.T3.2.9" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A2.T3.2.9.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;"><math id="A2.T3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Beta}(6,4)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">Beta</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">6</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">4</mn><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Beta}(6,4)</annotation></semantics></math></th>
<td id="A2.T3.2.9.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;"><math id="A2.T3.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.423\pm 0.004" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">0.423</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">0.004</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.423\pm 0.004</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A2.T3.2.9.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;"><math id="A2.T3.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.332" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn mathsize="0.900em">0.332</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.332</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Prior-mismatch robustness at <math id="A2.T3.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=10</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.T3.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=8</annotation></semantics></math></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Under sparsity mismatch, DABS beats the static baseline at every evaluation <math id="A2.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> except <math id="A2.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi=0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi=0.2</annotation></semantics></math> (which matches the training-prior mean and yields a tie). The absolute F1 of both arms grows with <math id="A2.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, because a higher active-factor base rate inflates F1 for any competent policy. The gap over the static baseline stays positive and grows at high <math id="A2.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>: at <math id="A2.SS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, DABS reaches F1 <math id="A2.SS3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=0.410" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>0.410</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=0.410</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A2.SS3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.343" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.343</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.343</annotation></semantics></math> for the static design. This concentration advantage does not require the sparsity of the training prior to match that of the evaluation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The Beta hyperprior mismatch tells a similar story. Under the matched Beta<math id="A2.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(2,8)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2,8)</annotation></semantics></math> prior, DABS beats the static design by <math id="A2.SS3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.054" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.054</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.054</annotation></semantics></math>. Under Beta<math id="A2.SS3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(4,6)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4,6)</annotation></semantics></math> the gap narrows to <math id="A2.SS3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.029" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.029</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.029</annotation></semantics></math>. Under Beta<math id="A2.SS3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(6,4)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(6,4)</annotation></semantics></math>, which biases the prior toward many-active configurations, the gap widens to <math id="A2.SS3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.090" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.090</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.090</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that absolute F1 grows in both arms as the evaluation prior shifts toward denser configurations, because a higher base rate of actives inflates F1 for any competent policy. What matters for robustness is that DABS’ advantage over the static baseline is preserved (and actually widens at Beta<math id="A2.SS3.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(6,4)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(6,4)</annotation></semantics></math>) across the tested mismatches. DABS is therefore robust to a misspecified sparsity prior.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Derivation of the joint distribution of the history</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We derive the closed form of the integral introduced in
Eq. <a href="#S3.E10" title="In 3.2 Analytical Marginalisation ‣ 3 Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>,</p>
<table id="A3.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(h_{T}\mid z)\;=\;\iint p(h_{T}\mid z,\beta,\sigma^{2})\,p(\beta\mid z)\,p(\sigma^{2})\,d\beta\,d\sigma^{2}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.391em">=</mo><mrow><mo>∬</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(h_{T}\mid z)\;=\;\iint p(h_{T}\mid z,\beta,\sigma^{2})\,p(\beta\mid z)\,p(\sigma^{2})\,d\beta\,d\sigma^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the parameter vector <math id="A3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=(z,\beta,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=(z,\beta,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> is decomposed
into the discrete activity indicators <math id="A3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, the continuous effect sizes
<math id="A3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, and the noise variance <math id="A3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Conditioning on <math id="A3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, we
integrate out <math id="A3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> analytically by exploiting the conjugate
normal–inverse-gamma structure of the prior.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Model specification</h3>

<div id="A3.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A3.SSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}=(y_{1},\dots,y_{T})^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}=(y_{1},\dots,y_{T})^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{T}</annotation></semantics></math> collect the observed responses in history <math id="A3.SSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{T}=\{(\xi_{t},y_{t})\}_{t=1}^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{T}=\{(\xi_{t},y_{t})\}_{t=1}^{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="A3.SSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times p}</annotation></semantics></math> be the design matrix with rows <math id="A3.SSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{t}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{t}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>. Given the activity pattern <math id="A3.SSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A3.SSx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{z}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times p_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{z}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times p_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the submatrix of active columns, where <math id="A3.SSx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{z}=\sum_{k}z_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{z}=\sum_{k}z_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of active factors. The hierarchical model conditioned on <math id="A3.SSx1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> is:</p>
<table id="A3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.E19"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbf{y}\mid\beta_{z},\sigma^{2},z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{y}\mid\beta_{z},\sigma^{2},z</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E19.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\;\sim\;\mathcal{N}(X_{z}\beta_{z},\;\sigma^{2}I_{T})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\;\sim\;\mathcal{N}(X_{z}\beta_{z},\;\sigma^{2}I_{T}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A3.E20"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\beta_{z}\mid\sigma^{2},z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\beta_{z}\mid\sigma^{2},z</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E20.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\;\sim\;\mathcal{N}(0,\;\sigma^{2}\tau_{z}^{2}I_{p_{z}})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\;\sim\;\mathcal{N}(0,\;\sigma^{2}\tau_{z}^{2}I_{p_{z}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SSx1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SSx1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{0},\beta_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{0},\beta_{0})</annotation></semantics></math> are the inverse-gamma hyperparameters
introduced in Section 3.1. This normal–inverse-gamma specification is the
conjugate prior for the Gaussian likelihood, enabling both integrals to be
computed in closed form.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Step 1: Integrating out <math id="A3.SSx2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{z}</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="A3.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since the likelihood equation <a href="#A3.E19" title="In Model specification ‣ Appendix C Derivation of the joint distribution of the history ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> and the prior
equation <a href="#A3.E20" title="In Model specification ‣ Appendix C Derivation of the joint distribution of the history ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> are both Gaussian conditionally on <math id="A3.SSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>,
standard Gaussian identities give</p>

<p id="A3.SSx2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{z}:=I_{T}+\tau_{z}^{2}X_{z}X_{z}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{z}:=I_{T}+\tau_{z}^{2}X_{z}X_{z}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> encodes the covariance
structure induced by the active set <math id="A3.SSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> through <math id="A3.SSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{z}</annotation></semantics></math>. Explicitly:</p>

<section id="A3.SSx3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Step 2: Integrating out <math id="A3.SSx3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="A3.SSx3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now integrate equation <a href="#A3.E23" title="In Step 1: Integrating out 𝛽_𝑧 ‣ Appendix C Derivation of the joint distribution of the history ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> against the
<math id="A3.SSx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{IG}(\alpha_{0},\beta_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>IG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{IG}(\alpha_{0},\beta_{0})</annotation></semantics></math> prior on <math id="A3.SSx3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Collecting powers
of <math id="A3.SSx3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{\infty}p(\mathbf{y}\mid\sigma^{2},z)\,p(\sigma^{2})\,d\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{\infty}p(\mathbf{y}\mid\sigma^{2},z)\,p(\sigma^{2})\,d\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A3.SSx3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The integrand is an inverse-gamma kernel with updated parameters</p>
<table id="A3.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{T}\;:=\;\alpha_{0}+\frac{T}{2},\qquad\beta_{T}\;:=\;\beta_{0}+\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbf{y}^{\top}\Sigma_{z}^{-1}\mathbf{y}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.558em">:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐲</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{T}\;:=\;\alpha_{0}+\frac{T}{2},\qquad\beta_{T}\;:=\;\beta_{0}+\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbf{y}^{\top}\Sigma_{z}^{-1}\mathbf{y},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SSx3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">so the integral evaluates to <math id="A3.SSx3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma(\alpha_{T})/\beta_{T}^{\alpha_{T}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mi>β</mi><mi>T</mi><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma(\alpha_{T})/\beta_{T}^{\alpha_{T}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
yielding</p>
<table id="A3.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{y}\mid z)\;=\;\frac{\beta_{0}^{\alpha_{0}}\,\Gamma\!\left(\alpha_{0}+\frac{T}{2}\right)}{(2\pi)^{T/2}\,\Gamma(\alpha_{0})\,|\Sigma_{z}|^{1/2}}\left(\beta_{0}+\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbf{y}^{\top}\Sigma_{z}^{-1}\mathbf{y}\right)^{-\left(\alpha_{0}+\frac{T}{2}\right)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0.170em" lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{y}\mid <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SSx4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Step 3: Identifying the Student-<math id="A3.SSx4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> form</h3>

<div id="A3.SSx4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SSx4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Setting <math id="A3.SSx4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu:=2\alpha_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu:=2\alpha_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> (so the degrees of freedom are determined by
<math id="A3.SSx4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> alone) and defining the scale matrix</p>
<table id="A3.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.SSx4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">expression equation <a href="#A3.E26" title="In Step 2: Integrating out 𝜎^2 ‣ Appendix C Derivation of the joint distribution of the history ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">26</span></a> is exactly the density of the
multivariate Student-<math id="A3.SSx4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> stated in Section 3.1:</p>
<table id="A3.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(h_{T}\mid z)\;=\;\frac{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{\nu+T}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{\nu}{2}\right)(\nu\pi)^{T/2}\,|S_{z}|^{1/2}}\left(1+\frac{1}{\nu}\,\mathbf{y}^{\top}S_{z}^{-1}\mathbf{y}\right)^{-\frac{\nu+T}{2}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.SSx4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">confirming that <math id="A3.SSx4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{T}\mid z\sim\mathrm{St}_{\nu}(0,S_{z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>St</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{T}\mid z\sim\mathrm{St}_{\nu}(0,S_{z})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SSx4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SSx4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As stated in
Section 3.2, the degrees of freedom <math id="A3.SSx4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu=2\alpha_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu=2\alpha_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and the scale matrix
<math id="A3.SSx4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{z}</annotation></semantics></math> are jointly determined by the active set <math id="A3.SSx4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> (through <math id="A3.SSx4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{z}</annotation></semantics></math>), the
design matrix induced by the history, and the three prior hyperparameters <math id="A3.SSx4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{0},\beta_{0},\tau^{2}_{\mathrm{active}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>active</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{0},\beta_{0},\tau^{2}_{\mathrm{active}})</annotation></semantics></math>, together with the active-column selection induced by <math id="A3.SSx4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Encoder details</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The policy <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\phi}(\xi_{t}\mid h_{t-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi}(\xi_{t}\mid h_{t-1})</annotation></semantics></math> converts a variable-length history <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t-1}=\{(\xi_{s},y_{s})\}_{s=1}^{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t-1}=\{(\xi_{s},y_{s})\}_{s=1}^{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> into per-factor design logits <math id="A4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, subject to two structural requirements: invariance to the order of past experiments and a fixed-dimensional output independent of <math id="A4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All encoders we consider share the same two-stage pipeline:</p>
<ul id="A4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">an encoder first summarises the history into a fixed-length vector <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{enc}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>enc</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\mathrm{enc}}}</annotation></semantics></math>;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">an emitter MLP <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> then maps this summary to the logits <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math>. The emitter is a two-hidden-layer MLP with Softplus activations. At step <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math>, the encoder returns a learnable empty-history vector <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> initialised to zero.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">We first describe the sufficient-statistics encoder used in the main experiments, followed by a permutation-invariant set encoder used as an ablation baseline.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sufficient-statistics encoder (default).</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=p+\binom{p}{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=p+\binom{p}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the number of main-effect plus two-way-interaction columns, let <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{(t-1)\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{(t-1)\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> stack the past designs expanded with those columns, and let <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> collect the responses. Under the linear–Gaussian likelihood with conjugate Normal–Inverse-Gamma prior, the Student-<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> posterior over <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> depends on the history only through the sufficient statistics <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1},\ X_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1},\ y_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1},\ X_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1},\ y_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1})</annotation></semantics></math>. We assemble these statistics into the vector</p>
<table id="A4.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t-1}=\Big(\operatorname{vec}_{\triangle}\!\Big(\tfrac{X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1}}{T}\Big),\;\tfrac{X_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1}}{T},\;\tfrac{y_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1}}{T}\Big)\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d(d+1)}{2}+d+1}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">△</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mi>T</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mi>T</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo>,</mo><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mi>T</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t-1}=\Big(\operatorname{vec}_{\triangle}\!\Big(\tfrac{X_{t-1}^{\top}X_{t-1}}{T}\Big),\;\tfrac{X_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1}}{T},\;\tfrac{y_{t-1}^{\top}y_{t-1}}{T}\Big)\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d(d+1)}{2}+d+1},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(29)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{vec}_{\triangle}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">△</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{vec}_{\triangle}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> extracts the upper-triangular entries of the symmetric matrix.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The normalisation by <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> produces dimensionless inputs. For <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1</annotation></semantics></math> designs it maps diagonal entries of <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X^{\top}X/T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X^{\top}X/T</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> and off-diagonals to <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. The statistic vector is then mapped to the encoding by a projection head</p>
<table id="A4.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\mathrm{proj}}=\mathrm{Linear}\circ\mathrm{Softplus}\circ\mathrm{Linear}\circ\mathrm{LayerNorm}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>proj</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Linear</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>Softplus</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>Linear</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>LayerNorm</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\mathrm{proj}}=\mathrm{Linear}\circ\mathrm{Softplus}\circ\mathrm{Linear}\circ\mathrm{LayerNorm}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">with encoding width <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{enc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>enc</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{enc}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Permutation invariance over past experiments holds by construction since each statistic is a symmetric function of the pairs <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\xi_{s},y_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\xi_{s},y_{s})</annotation></semantics></math>, and the output dimension is constant in <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>. The statistic dimension grows as <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(d^{2})=\mathcal{O}(p^{4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(d^{2})=\mathcal{O}(p^{4})</annotation></semantics></math>, which is tractable for the problem sizes considered here but not immediately scalable to very high-dimensional screening.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Set encoder (ablation baseline).</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For comparison we also implement the set-equivariant encoder used by DAD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Foster et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. Each pair <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\xi_{s},y_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\xi_{s},y_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> is concatenated with sinusoidal positional features of the step index <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> and mapped through a shared single-hidden-layer MLP <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> to a per-step embedding. The embeddings are then summed:</p>
<table id="A4.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{s}=\psi_{\phi}\big([\xi_{s};\ y_{s};\ \mathrm{PE}(s)]\big),\qquad c_{t-1}=\sum_{s=1}^{t-1}e_{s}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.667em">;</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.667em">;</mo><mrow><mi>PE</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{s}=\psi_{\phi}\big([\xi_{s};\ y_{s};\ \mathrm{PE}(s)]\big),\qquad c_{t-1}=\sum_{s=1}^{t-1}e_{s}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(30)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We use Softplus activation, a LayerNorm on the output to bound each contribution to a fixed magnitude, and sinusoidal positional features over <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{pe}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>pe</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{pe}}</annotation></semantics></math> frequency scales. Permutation invariance over the multiset holds because the summation is commutative. In principle this encoder is fully general as it does not assume sufficiency, but the per-pair MLP must learn to approximate the sufficient statistics from data, which we find is less sample-efficient in our experiments than computing the statistics directly.</p>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<div id="alg1.l7" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
            <span id="alg1.l7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <math id="alg1.l7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1,\dots,T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1,\dots,T</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l8" class="ltx_listingline">

</div>
<div id="alg1.l17" class="ltx_listingline">
            
            
            <math id="alg1.l17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(\phi)\leftarrow\tfrac{1}{B}\sum_{b=1}^{B}\left[-\widehat{\mathrm{sPCE}}_{L}^{(b)}(\phi)\right]+\mu\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{L2}}(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>B</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>sPCE</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>L2</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(\phi)\leftarrow\tfrac{1}{B}\sum_{b=1}^{B}\left[-\widehat{\mathrm{sPCE}}_{L}^{(b)}(\phi)\right]+\mu\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{L2}}(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>

            <span id="alg1.l18.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Update:</span> <math id="alg1.l18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi\leftarrow\phi-\eta\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi\leftarrow\phi-\eta\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math>

<div id="alg2.l13" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg2.l13.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">13:</span></span>
            
            
          <span id="alg2.l13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <math id="alg2.l13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=1,\dots,G+N_{\mathrm{burn}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>burn</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=1,\dots,G+N_{\mathrm{burn}}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg2.l13.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span>

            <span id="alg2.l14.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Step B (update <math id="alg2.l14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>):</span> Sample <math id="alg2.l14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{k}^{(g)}\mid z_{-k}^{(g-1)},h_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{k}^{(g)}\mid z_{-k}^{(g-1)},h_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="alg2.l14.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1,\dots,p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1,\dots,p</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg2.l14.4" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="alg2.l14.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Student-<math id="alg2.l14.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> marginal, Eq. <a href="#A7.E36" title="In Step B: sampling 𝑧_𝑘|{𝑧_{-𝑘},ℎ_𝑇}. ‣ Appendix G Posterior inference details ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">36</span></a>
</span>

<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Posterior inference details</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide details of the Gibbs sampler used to approximate the posterior distribution <math id="A7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(z,\beta\mid h_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z,\beta\mid h_{T})</annotation></semantics></math> under the spike-and-slab prior and Gaussian likelihood. Let <math id="A7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the design matrix including main effects and interaction terms, where <math id="A7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=p+\binom{p}{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=p+\binom{p}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="A7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y\in\mathbb{R}^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\in\mathbb{R}^{T}</annotation></semantics></math> collect the observed responses. The likelihood is</p>
<table id="A7.E31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y\mid\beta,\sigma^{2}\sim\mathcal{N}(X\beta,\sigma^{2}I)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\mid\beta,\sigma^{2}\sim\mathcal{N}(X\beta,\sigma^{2}I).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(31)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The prior over coefficients is given by a spike-and-slab distribution:</p>
<table id="A7.E32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E32.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{k}\mid z_{k},\sigma^{2}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}\,\tau_{z_{k}}^{2}),\qquad z_{k}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\rho)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Bernoulli</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{k}\mid z_{k},\sigma^{2}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}\,\tau_{z_{k}}^{2}),\qquad z_{k}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\rho),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(32)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{z_{k}}^{2}=\tau_{\mathrm{active}}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>active</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{z_{k}}^{2}=\tau_{\mathrm{active}}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="A7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{k}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{k}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{z_{k}}^{2}=\tau_{\mathrm{inactive}}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>inactive</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{z_{k}}^{2}=\tau_{\mathrm{inactive}}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="A7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{k}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{k}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Interaction indicators follow the strong-heredity constraint of Section 3.1, <math id="A7.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{ij}\mid z_{i},z_{j}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\pi_{\mathrm{int}}\,z_{i}z_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Bernoulli</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>int</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{ij}\mid z_{i},z_{j}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\pi_{\mathrm{int}}\,z_{i}z_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>, which reduces to <math id="A7.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{ij}=z_{i}z_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{ij}=z_{i}z_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> in the deterministic limit <math id="A7.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\mathrm{int}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>int</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\mathrm{int}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>. The prior variance vector <math id="A7.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{z}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{z}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> concatenates the main-effect variances and the heredity-derived interaction variances.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Direct posterior computation is intractable due to the combinatorial structure of <math id="A7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\in\{0,1\}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\in\{0,1\}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math>. We therefore employ a Gibbs sampler that alternates between sampling <math id="A7.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A7.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> from their conditional distributions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The primary inferential targets are the posterior activity probability for each factor <math id="A7.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> and the corresponding effect-size estimate, computed from <math id="A7.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> post-burn-in Gibbs samples as</p>
<table id="A7.E33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}(z_{k}=1\mid h_{T})=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}z_{k}^{(g)},\qquad\hat{\beta}_{k}=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}\beta_{k}^{(g)}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>G</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>G</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>β</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}(z_{k}=1\mid h_{T})=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}z_{k}^{(g)},\qquad\hat{\beta}_{k}=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}\beta_{k}^{(g)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(33)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A7.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{k}^{(g)}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{k}^{(g)}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{k}^{(g)}\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>β</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{k}^{(g)}\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> are the samples at Gibbs iteration <math id="A7.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>. A factor <math id="A7.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> is declared active if</p>
<table id="A7.E34" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}(z_{k}=1\mid h_{T})&gt;0.5," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}(z_{k}=1\mid h_{T})&gt;0.5,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(34)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.p4.3" class="ltx_p">and <math id="A7.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> credible intervals are obtained from the empirical quantiles of <math id="A7.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\beta_{k}^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>β</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\beta_{k}^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chipman et al., 1997</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Step A: sampling <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\mid z,\sigma^{2},h_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\mid z,\sigma^{2},h_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{z}^{-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{z}^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the prior precision vector under activity pattern <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>. Given the current <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> sample from Step C, and conditioned on <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, the prior on <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> is a diagonal Gaussian and the likelihood is linear–Gaussian. By Normal–Normal conjugacy the posterior is</p>

<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Step B: sampling <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{k}\mid z_{-k},h_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{k}\mid z_{-k},h_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each factor <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{-k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{-k}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes all activity indicators except <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, the conditional posterior is a Bernoulli whose probability is obtained by marginalising <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> analytically:</p>

</table>
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> is the prior activity probability defined in Eq. <a href="#S3.E7" title="In 3.1 Problem Setup and Factorial Screening Model ‣ 3 Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> and the marginal likelihood is available in closed form:</p>

<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">This closed-form Student-<math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> marginal arises under the conjugate g-prior coupling <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\mid\sigma^{2},z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}\,\mathrm{diag}(\tau_{z}^{2}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>diag</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\mid\sigma^{2},z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}\,\mathrm{diag}(\tau_{z}^{2}))</annotation></semantics></math>, which we adopt throughout as a tight approximation of the exact marginal under the independent-normal prior of Section 3.1 (see Section 3.2).</p>
