</section>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Step C: sampling <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}\mid\beta,z,h_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}\mid\beta,z,h_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Conditional on <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, the noise variance has an inverse-gamma conditional posterior:</p>
<table id="A7.E38" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E38.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}\mid\beta,z,h_{T}\sim\mathrm{InvGamma}\!\left(\alpha_{0}+\tfrac{T}{2},\ \beta_{0}+\tfrac{1}{2}\,\|y-X\beta\|_{2}^{2}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:5.068em;" width="5.068em"><mi>InvGamma</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}\mid\beta,z,h_{T}\sim\mathrm{InvGamma}\!\left(\alpha_{0}+\tfrac{T}{2},\ \beta_{0}+\tfrac{1}{2}\,\|y-X\beta\|_{2}^{2}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(38)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The current <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> sample is required in Step A. The <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-update of Step B uses the Student-<math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> marginal of Eq. <a href="#A7.E37" title="In Step B: sampling 𝑧_𝑘|{𝑧_{-𝑘},ℎ_𝑇}. ‣ Appendix G Posterior inference details ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">37</span></a>, which already integrates <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> out analytically and therefore does not require the current <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> value.</p>
</div>

</section>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Extended case study results</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix reports the metric curves that did not appear in the main text for each of the three case studies of Section 5. In each subsection, the figures use the same DABS and baseline colour scheme as the corresponding main-text figures and share the same random-seed protocol (five seeds per <math id="A8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(p,T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(p,T)</annotation></semantics></math> cell, 95% confidence intervals).</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.1 </span>Case Study 1: biotechnology benchmark (main effects, <math id="A8.SS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> sweep at <math id="A8.SS1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=15</annotation></semantics></math>)</h3>

<div id="A8.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 5.2 reports F1 and TPR versus the budget <math id="A8.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A8.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=15</annotation></semantics></math>. Figure <a href="#A8.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ H.1 Case Study 1: biotechnology benchmark (main effects, 𝑇 sweep at 𝑝=15) ‣ Appendix H Extended case study results ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> completes the picture with the corresponding FDR curves.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.16927v1/fig_5_1_baselines_FDR.png" id="A8.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:454/277;" width="454" height="277" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span>Main-effect FDR versus budget <math id="A8.F7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A8.F7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=15</annotation></semantics></math> for the biotechnology benchmark</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A8.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A8.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ H.1 Case Study 1: biotechnology benchmark (main effects, 𝑇 sweep at 𝑝=15) ‣ Appendix H Extended case study results ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> shows main-effect FDR versus the budget <math id="A8.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>. The two Bayesian arms (DABS and the static design) achieve substantially lower FDR than the non-Bayesian baselines across the sweep. Multi-stage adaptive maintains an FDR between <math id="A8.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.27" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.27</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.27</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.49</annotation></semantics></math>, and Plackett-Burman reaches <math id="A8.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.42</annotation></semantics></math> at its native <math id="A8.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math>. Between the two Bayesian arms, the static design achieves lower FDR at the smallest budgets, but this reflects its very low recall in that regime (recall F1 <math id="A8.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=0.03</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A8.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=4</annotation></semantics></math> from Section 5.2): the static design predicts almost no actives at all, so its false-positive rate is low by default. Above the identifiability boundary, DABS and the static design converge to comparable FDR values around <math id="A8.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.10</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A8.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math>, consistent with the wedge prediction of Section 3.6.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.2 </span>Case Study 2: HSC benchmark (main effects, <math id="A8.SS2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> sweep at <math id="A8.SS2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math>)</h3>

<div id="A8.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 5.3 reports F1 and FDR versus <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> at fixed <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math>. Figure <a href="#A8.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ H.2 Case Study 2: HSC benchmark (main effects, 𝑝 sweep at 𝑇=16) ‣ Appendix H Extended case study results ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> completes the picture with the true positive rate for the same sweep.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.16927v1/fig_5_2_baselines_TPR.png" id="A8.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:454/277;" width="454" height="277" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span>Main-effect TPR versus number of candidate factors <math id="A8.F8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A8.F8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math> for the HSC benchmark. Bands are 95% CIs over 5 seeds.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A8.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">TPR declines for every method as <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> grows, as the fixed budget <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math> is spread over an increasing number of candidate factors. In the identifiable regime <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\leq 15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\leq 15</annotation></semantics></math>, all methods except multi-stage adaptive achieve TPR between 0.5 and 0.7, with Plackett-Burman competitive up to its native <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=15</annotation></semantics></math>. From <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=18</annotation></semantics></math> onward, DABS and the static design track each other closely (TPR between 0.51 and 0.60) and both stay above the myopic baseline, which degrades faster with <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> (0.41 at <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=26" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>26</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=26</annotation></semantics></math>). Multi-stage adaptive stays near 0.30 throughout, well below the other methods. Its multi-stage pruning discards candidates aggressively at each stage, so recall on the active set remains low regardless of <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.3 </span>Case Study 3: metallurgical benchmark (main effects + interactions, <math id="A8.SS3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> sweep at <math id="A8.SS3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in\{4,6,8\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in\{4,6,8\}</annotation></semantics></math>)</h3>

<div id="A8.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 5.4 reports F1 for main effects and two-factor interactions across the three problem sizes. Figures <a href="#A8.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ H.3 Case Study 3: metallurgical benchmark (main effects + interactions, 𝑇 sweep at 𝑝∈{4,6,8}) ‣ Appendix H Extended case study results ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>–<a href="#A8.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ H.3 Case Study 3: metallurgical benchmark (main effects + interactions, 𝑇 sweep at 𝑝∈{4,6,8}) ‣ Appendix H Extended case study results ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> complete the picture with the corresponding TPR and FDR curves.</p>
</div>

</figure>

</figure>

</figure>
<figure id="A8.F12" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.16927v1/fig_5_3_baselines_FDR_int.png" id="A8.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:648/186;" width="648" height="186" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 12: </span>Two-factor interaction FDR versus budget <math id="A8.F12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> across <math id="A8.F12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in\{4,6,8\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in\{4,6,8\}</annotation></semantics></math></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A8.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Main-effect TPR and FDR behave as ceiling metrics for the two amortised policies, mirroring the F1 story of Section 5.4: DABS and the static design track each other closely, both above the myopic baseline. The interaction TPR and FDR curves show a clearer three-way separation at <math id="A8.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=6</annotation></semantics></math> in the mid-budget window, again matching the F1 pattern. At <math id="A8.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=8</annotation></semantics></math>, DABS and the static design maintain their advantage over the myopic baseline on both interaction metrics, while their own curves converge at the high-budget end of the sweep as the interaction problem approaches its own identifiability ceiling.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>On the use of implicit DAD (iDAD)</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent work has proposed implicit Deep Adaptive Design (iDAD) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ivanova et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, which replaces explicit likelihood evaluation in the expected information gain objective with a learned critic network and enables amortized design optimization in simulator-based settings with intractable likelihoods.</p>
</div>
<div id="A9.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In our setting, however, the model admits a conjugate Normal–Inverse-Gamma prior with a linear Gaussian likelihood, yielding a closed-form Student-<math id="A9.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> marginal likelihood. This quantity can therefore be evaluated exactly within the prior-contrastive estimator.</p>
</div>
<div id="A9.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p3.1" class="ltx_p">As a result, adopting iDAD would replace an exact computation with a learned approximation, introducing additional estimator variance and potential bias without a compensating benefit. We therefore retain an explicit likelihood formulation throughout.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Result details and discussion</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix collects the exact hyperparameters, architectures, and evaluation settings used across the three case studies of Section 5. Unless stated otherwise, all DABS runs use the sufficient-statistics encoder (Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Encoder details ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>) with a two-hidden-layer MLP emitter, and all training uses stochastic gradient descent on the combined objective <math id="A10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(\phi)=-\widehat{\mathrm{sPCE}}_{L}(\phi)+\mu\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{L2}}(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>sPCE</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>L2</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(\phi)=-\widehat{\mathrm{sPCE}}_{L}(\phi)+\mu\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{L2}}(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math> defined in Section 3.2.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A10.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Appendix J Result details and discussion ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> summarises the model priors, training schedule, and evaluation protocol for each case study.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A10.T4" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A10.T4.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A10.T4.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A10.T4.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"></th>
<td id="A10.T4.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A10.T4.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Case Study 1</span></td>
<td id="A10.T4.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A10.T4.2.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Case Study 2</span></td>
<td id="A10.T4.2.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A10.T4.2.1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Case Study 3</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A10.T4.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A10.T4.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_th ltx_th_row"></th>

</figure>
<div id="A10.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The Plackett-Burman baseline uses the native run counts <math id="A10.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\in\{8,12,16,20,24\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\in\{8,12,16,20,24\}</annotation></semantics></math> for its 12-, 16-, 20-, and 24-run constructions. The myopic baseline shares the same Bayesian model and Gibbs decoder as DABS. At each step it evaluates the one-step expected information gain over a candidate set of enumerated (small <math id="A10.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>) or randomly sampled (<math id="A10.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 10</annotation></semantics></math>) designs and selects the maximiser. The multi-stage adaptive baseline runs <math id="A10.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=3</annotation></semantics></math> stages with keep-fraction <math id="A10.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, using ridge-regularised linear estimates of marginal effects to prune inactive candidates between stages.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.p4.1" class="ltx_p">All experiments were run on NVIDIA H100 80GB GPUs on a university HPC cluster. A typical DABS training run takes approximately 10 minutes at <math id="A10.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=8</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A10.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=8</annotation></semantics></math>, and roughly 45 minutes at <math id="A10.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=20</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A10.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math>. Evaluation with the Gibbs sampler takes approximately 5 minutes per checkpoint on CPU. Each reported F1, TPR, and FDR value is the mean over 50 rollouts computed independently for each of the 5 training seeds.</p>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A11" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix K </span>Visualisation of adaptive behaviour</h2>

<div id="A11.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To illustrate the behaviour of the learned policy, Figure <a href="#A11.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ Appendix K Visualisation of adaptive behaviour ‣ Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> shows a single rollout of the sequential design process. Panel (a) displays the sequence of selected designs <math id="A11.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{t,k}\in\{-1,+1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{t,k}\in\{-1,+1\}</annotation></semantics></math>, where rows correspond to experiments and columns to factors. The early designs exhibit substantial variability across factors, reflecting an exploratory phase. As data are collected, the designs become more structured, with repeated interventions on a subset of factors, indicating a shift toward exploiting informative directions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Panel (b) shows the evolution of the posterior inclusion probabilities <math id="A11.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(z_{k}=1|h_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(z_{k}=1|h_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>. Starting from a diffuse prior, the posterior progressively concentrates, with one factor emerging as clearly active while the others are shrunk toward low inclusion probabilities.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Panel (c) presents the posterior distribution of the effect sizes at the final step <math id="A11.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=T</annotation></semantics></math>, including posterior means and 95% credible intervals. The active factor is accurately identified, while inactive effects are effectively shrunk toward zero.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Together, these panels illustrate how the policy adapts over time, transitioning from broad exploration to targeted experimentation, and enabling reliable recovery of the sparse active set.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A11.F13" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.16927v1/rollout_visualisation.png" id="A11.F13.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:648/198;" width="648" height="198" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 13: </span>Illustration of adaptive behavior in a single rollout</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</article>
